Main.sentence: Air Force One is the official ___E:air traffic control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_traffic_control)___ -designated ___E:call sign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation_call_signs)___ for a ___E:United States Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force)___ aircraft carrying the ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ .
The term is commonly used to denote U.S.

Air Force aircraft modified and used to transport the president, and as a ___E:metonym U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metonym)___ for the primary presidential aircraft, ___E:VC-25 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_VC-25)___ , although it can be used to refer to any Air Force aircraft the president travels on.

The idea of designating specific ___E:military aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_aircraft)___ to ___E:transport the president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transportation_of_the_President_of_the_United_States)___ arose during ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ when military advisors in the ___E:War Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_War)___ were concerned about the risk of using commercial airlines for presidential travel.
In 1944, a ___E:C-54 Skymaster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_C-54_Skymaster)___ was converted for use as the first purpose-built presidential aircraft.

Dubbed the Sacred Cow and operated by the ___E:Army Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces)___ , it carried President ___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ to the ___E:Yalta Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalta_Conference)___ in February 1945 and was used for another two years by President ___E:Harry S. Truman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman)___ .

The "Air Force One" ___E:call sign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_call_sign)___ was created in 1954, after a ___E:Lockheed Constellation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Constellation)___ carrying President ___E:Dwight D. Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower)___ entered the same airspace as a commercial airline flight using the same ___E:flight number U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_number)___ .

Since the introduction of SAM 26000 in 1962, the primary presidential aircraft has carried the distinctive ___E:livery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_livery)___ designed by ___E:Raymond Loewy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Loewy)___ .

Other aircraft designated as Air Force One have included another Lockheed Constellation, Columbine III ; three ___E:Boeing 707s U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_707)___ , introduced in the 1960s and 1970s; and the current ___E:Boeing VC-25As U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_VC-25)___ .
Since 1990, the presidential fleet has consisted of two highly customized ___E:Boeing 747-200B U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_747-200#747-200)___ (VC-25A) aircraft.

The USAF has ordered two ___E:Boeing 747-8s U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_747-8)___ to serve as the next presidential aircraft, designated VC-25Bs and expected to enter service no earlier than 2026.

From time to time, presidents have invited other world leaders to travel with them on Air Force One. In 1973, President Nixon invited ___E:Soviet general secretary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union)___ ___E:Leonid Brezhnev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Brezhnev)___ to fly with him to California from Washington, D.C.

In 1983, President Reagan and ___E:Queen Elizabeth II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II)___ toured the ___E:U.S. West Coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast_of_the_United_States)___ aboard the aircraft.

On 11 October 1910, ___E:Theodore Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt)___ became the first US president to fly in an aircraft, an early ___E:Wright Flyer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_Flyer)___ from ___E:Kinloch Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambert%E2%80%93St._Louis_International_Airport)___ near ___E:St. Louis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis)___ , ___E:Missouri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri)___ .
He was no longer in office at the time, having been succeeded by ___E:William Howard Taft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft)___ .
The record-making occasion was a brief overflight of the crowd at a county fair but was nonetheless the beginning of presidential air travel.
___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ was the first president to fly in an aircraft while in office.

The first aircraft obtained specifically for presidential travel was a ___E:Douglas Dolphin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_Dolphin)___ ___E:amphibian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibious_aircraft)___ modified with luxury upholstery for four passengers and a small separate sleeping compartment.
Designated RD-2 by the US Navy, it was delivered in 1933 and based at the ___E:naval base at Anacostia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Support_Facility_Anacostia)___ in Washington, D.C.
The aircraft remained in service as a presidential transport from 1939.

During World War II, German submarines ___E:operating in the Atlantic Ocean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Atlantic)___ made air travel the preferred method of VIP transatlantic transportation.

In 1943, Roosevelt traveled to the ___E:Casablanca Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casablanca_Conference_(1943))___ in Morocco on the Dixie Clipper , a Pan Am-crewed ___E:Boeing 314 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_314)___ ___E:flying boat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_boat)___ , on a flight that covered 5,500 miles (8,890 km) in three legs.

Concerned about relying upon commercial airlines to transport the president, officials of the ___E:United States Army Air Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces)___ , the predecessor of the US Air Force, ordered the conversion of a military aircraft to accommodate the special needs of the ___E:commander-in-chief U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-chief#United_States)___ .

In 1943, a ___E:C-87A U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidated_C-87_Liberator_Express)___ transport, number 41-24159, was modified to carry President Franklin D. Roosevelt on international trips.
But after a review of the C-87's controversial safety record, the Secret Service flatly refused to approve the aircraft for presidential carriage.

The C-87, a derivative of the ___E:Consolidated B-24 Liberator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidated_B-24_Liberator)___ bomber, also carried more militaristic associations than aircraft designed for transport.
The aircraft, named Guess Where II , was used to transport senior members of the Roosevelt administration on various trips.
In March 1944, it flew ___E:Eleanor Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleanor_Roosevelt)___ on a goodwill tour of several Latin American countries.
The C-87 was scrapped in 1945.

The Secret Service subsequently reconfigured a Douglas ___E:C-54 Skymaster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-54_Skymaster)___ for presidential transport duty. The VC-54C aircraft, nicknamed the Sacred Cow , included a ___E:sleeping area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_cabin)___ , ___E:radiotelephone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiotelephone)___ , and retractable battery-powered ___E:elevator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevator)___ to lift Roosevelt in his wheelchair.
The VC-54C flew President Roosevelt only once, to the ___E:Yalta Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalta_Conference)___ in February 1945.

The ___E:National Security Act of 1947 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Act_of_1947)___ , the legislation that created the US Air Force, was signed by President ___E:Harry S. Truman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman)___ aboard the VC-54C.
He replaced the VC-54C in 1947 with a modified ___E:C-118 Liftmaster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_DC-6)___ , calling it the Independence after his Missouri hometown.
It was given a distinctive exterior, as its nose was painted like the head of a ___E:bald eagle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bald_eagle)___ .
The plane included a stateroom in the aft fuselage and a main cabin that could seat 24 passengers or could be made up into 12 sleeper berths.

It is now housed at the ___E:National Museum of the United States Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_the_United_States_Air_Force)___ in ___E:Dayton, Ohio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio)___ .
Eisenhower introduced four propeller-driven aircraft to presidential service.
This group included two ___E:Lockheed C-121 Constellations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Constellation)___ : aircraft Columbine II (VC-121A 48-610)    and Columbine III (VC-121E 53-7885).

They were named by ___E:First Lady U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Mamie Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamie_Eisenhower)___ for the ___E:columbine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquilegia_coerulea)___ , official state flower of her adopted home state of ___E:Colorado U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado)___ .
Two ___E:Aero Commanders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aero_Commander_500)___ were also added to the fleet.

Columbine II is the first plane to bear the ___E:call sign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_sign)___ Air Force One, it was Lockheed Constellation configured for VIP travel and replaced an earlier Constellation called Columbine .

This designation for the US Air Force aircraft carrying the incumbent president was established after a 1954 incident in which a commercial flight, ___E:Eastern Air Lines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Air_Lines)___ 8610, crossed paths with Air Force 8610, which was carrying President Eisenhower.
Initially used informally, the designation became official in 1962.

Toward the end of Eisenhower's second term, Secretary of State ___E:John Foster Dulles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Foster_Dulles)___ commented that Soviet premier ___E:Nikita Khrushchev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev)___ and other senior Soviet officials had begun using the technologically advanced ___E:Tupolev Tu-114 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tupolev_Tu-114)___ aircraft for their travels, and it was no longer dignified for the president to fly in a propeller-driven aircraft.

This paved the way for the Air Force's initial procurement of three ___E:Boeing 707 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_C-137_Stratoliner)___ -120 (VC-137A) ___E:jet aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jet_aircraft)___ , designated SAM (Special Air Missions) 970, 971 and 972 .

The high-speed ___E:jet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jet_engine)___ technology built into these aircraft enabled presidents from Eisenhower through Nixon to travel long distances more quickly for face-to-face meetings with world leaders.

Then-Vice President ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ first used a VC-137A on his visit to Russia in July 1959 for the ___E:Kitchen Debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitchen_Debate)___ .

The following month, Eisenhower became the first president to fly via jet airplane when he used SAM 970 , nicknamed "Queenie" , to meet German Chancellor ___E:Konrad Adenauer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Adenauer)___ .

During Eisenhower's " ___E:Flight to Peace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_policy_of_the_Dwight_D._Eisenhower_administration#International_trips)___ " goodwill tour in December 1959, he visited 11 Asian nations, flying 22,000 miles (35,000 km) in 19 days, twice as fast as he could have covered that distance in one of the Columbines .
SAM 970 to SAM 972 were removed from the presidential role with the early-1960s arrival of the specially built VC-137C designated SAM 26000 .
The older planes were repainted in the Loewy secondary livery designed for ___E:Air Force Two U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Two)___ and other non-presidential VIP aircraft.
SAM 970 is now on display at ___E:The Museum of Flight U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Museum_of_Flight)___ in ___E:Seattle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle)___ , Washington.

SAM 971 , best remembered for returning the Americans held during the ___E:Iran hostage crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_hostage_crisis#Release)___ in 1981, is on display at the ___E:Pima Air and Space Museum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pima_Air_and_Space_Museum)___ in ___E:Tucson, Arizona U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson,_Arizona)___ .
SAM 972 was scrapped in October 1996. [citation needed]

The new ___E:VC-137C U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_C-137_Stratoliner)___ was not yet modified for presidential service when ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ took office in 1961. On the recommendation of his wife, ___E:Jacqueline Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Kennedy)___ , he contacted the French-born American industrial designer ___E:Raymond Loewy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Loewy)___ for help in designing new livery and interiors for the VC-137C.

Loewy, who had seen SAM 970 , complained to a friend in the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ that it "had a garish orange nose and looked too much like a military plane", Air Force One historian and former Smithsonian curator Von Hardesty told ___E:CNN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN)___ .
He offered Kennedy his design consultation services free of charge.

Kennedy chose a red-and-gold design from one of Loewy's initial concept sketches, and asked him to render the design all in blue. Loewy also drew inspiration from the first printed copy of the ___E:United States Declaration of Independence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence)___ , suggesting the widely spaced and upper case "United States of America" legend in ___E:Caslon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caslon)___ typeface.

He chose to expose the polished aluminum fuselage on the bottom side and used two blues, ___E:steel blue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steel_blue)___ associated with the early republic and the presidency and a more contemporary water blue , to represent an America both rooted in the past and flying inexorably into the future.

The ___E:presidential seal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seal_of_the_President_of_the_United_States)___ was added to both sides of the fuselage near the nose and a large American flag was painted on the tail. Loewy's work won immediate praise from the president and the press.

The ___E:cheatline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_livery#Cheatline)___ suggested a sleek and horizontal image that mirrored America's ___E:Jet Age U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jet_Age)___ optimism and prosperity of the era, and today signifies its legacy and tradition.

Loewy's VC-137C livery was adapted for the larger ___E:VC-25A U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_VC-25)___ when it entered service in 1990, and the secondary variation (without the darker blue cheatline and cap over the cockpit) is still in use on USAF ___E:C-40 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_C-40_Clipper)___ , ___E:C-37 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulfstream_V#Variants)___ , ___E:C-32 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_C-32)___ , and ___E:C-20 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulfstream_IV#C-20F/G/H/J_military_variants)___ aircraft in standard (non-presidential) VIP configurations.

The presidential paint scheme can also be seen on ___E:Union Pacific 4141 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Pacific_4141)___ , the locomotive used in ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ 's funeral train.

Under ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ , presidential air travel entered the jet age.  Although he could use the Eisenhower-era jets for trips to Canada, France, ___E:Austria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria)___ , and the United Kingdom, when he came into office, his primary aircraft domestically was still a prop powered ___E:Douglas VC-118A Liftmaster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_DC-6#Surviving_aircraft)___ .

In October 1962, the modified long-range Boeing VC-137C Stratoliner SAM 26000 , featuring livery designed by Loewy, was delivered and immediately became an important element of the Kennedy administration's brand.
SAM 26000 was in service from 1962 to 1998, serving presidents Kennedy to ___E:Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ .

On 22 November 1963, SAM 26000 carried President Kennedy to Dallas, Texas, where it served as the backdrop as the Kennedys greeted well-wishers at Dallas's ___E:Love Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Love_Field)___ .

Later that afternoon, Kennedy was ___E:assassinated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_John_F._Kennedy)___ , and Vice President ___E:Lyndon Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_Johnson)___ assumed the office of president.
He took the ___E:oath of office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ aboard SAM 26000 before departing to Washington, D.C.
Later, in January 1973, SAM 26000 took Johnson's body home to Texas after his state funeral in Washington.

Johnson used SAM 26000 to travel extensively domestically and to visit troops in South Vietnam during the Vietnam War. SAM 26000 served President Nixon on several groundbreaking overseas voyages, including his famous ___E:visit to the People's Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Nixon_visit_to_China)___ in February 1972 and his trip to the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ later that year, both firsts for an American president.
Nixon dubbed the plane the "Spirit of '76" in honor of the forthcoming bicentennial of the United States; that logo was painted on both sides of the plane's nose.

SAM 26000 was replaced in December 1972 by another VC-137C, Special Air Mission 27000 , although SAM 26000 was relegated to non-presidential VIP status (and repainted without the darker blue cap and cheatline), it served as a backup to SAM 27000 until it was finally retired in 1998.
In June 1974, while President Nixon was on his way to a scheduled stop in ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ , Syrian fighter jets intercepted Air Force One to act as escorts.
The crew was not informed in advance, so took evasive action including a dive.
After announcing his intention to resign the presidency, Nixon boarded SAM 27000 (with call sign "Air Force One") to travel to California.

Colonel Ralph Albertazzie, then pilot of Air Force One, recounted that after ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ was sworn in as president, the plane had to be redesignated as SAM 27000 , indicating no president was on board the aircraft.

Over Jefferson City, Missouri, Albertazzie radioed: " ___E:Kansas City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri)___ , this was Air Force One. Will you change our call sign to Sierra Alpha Mike (SAM) 27000?" Back came the reply: "Roger, Sierra Alpha Mike 27000. Good luck to the president."

Though ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ 's two terms as president saw no major changes to Air Force One, the manufacture of the presidential aircraft version of the ___E:747 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_747)___ began during his presidency.

The USAF issued a ___E:request for proposal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Request_for_proposal)___ in 1985 for two wide-body aircraft with a minimum of three engines and an unrefueled range of 6,000 miles (9,700 km).

Boeing with the 747 and McDonnell Douglas with the ___E:DC-10 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonnell_Douglas_DC-10)___ submitted proposals, and the ___E:Reagan Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reagan_Administration)___ ordered two identical 747s to replace the aging 707 VC-137 variants he used.   The interior designs, drawn up by First Lady ___E:Nancy Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan)___ , were reminiscent of the ___E:American Southwest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Southwest)___ .

When President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ left office in January 2009, he flew to Texas in a VC-25 that used call sign SAM 28000, as it did not carry the current president of the United States.

Similar arrangements were made for former presidents ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ , ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ , and ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ . [citation needed] President ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ flew to his ___E:Mar-a-Lago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar-a-Lago)___ estate aboard Air Force One on the final day of his first presidency in January 2021.

After the deaths of former presidents ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ and Ronald Reagan, VC-25 aircraft flew their remains to their home states of ___E:Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan)___ and California, respectively. [citation needed]

On 27 April 2009, a low-flying VC-25 circled New York City for a ___E:photo-op U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photo-op)___ and ___E:training exercise U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_exercise)___ , alarming many New Yorkers.

During Joe Biden's ___E:2023 visit to Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_visit_by_Joe_Biden_to_Ukraine)___ , the Air Force One call sign was not used for the C-32 aircraft he flew to ___E:Poland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland)___ ; to increase secrecy, the call sign was SAM060 .
When flying with the President, Air Force One rarely flies alone.
It is often accompanied by a fleet of aircraft that can include the back-up VC-25, cargo aircraft, and tankers.

In such cases, up to half a dozen cargo aircraft, such as the ___E:Boeing C-17 Globemaster III U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_C-17_Globemaster_III)___ or the ___E:Lockheed C-5 Galaxy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_C-5_Galaxy)___ , precede AF1 by a couple days or more, bringing the ___E:presidential limousine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_state_car_(United_States))___ and ___E:Sikorsky VH-60 Black Hawk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikorsky_UH-60_Black_Hawk)___ helicopters, along with Secret Service personnel and several hundred maintenance crew. Longer trips are accompanied by tankers, such as the ___E:McDonnell Douglas KC-10 Extender U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonnell_Douglas_KC-10_Extender)___ , to limit the need to stop for fuel and ensure that AF1 does not take fuel from an unvetted source.

The support aircraft will often use several airports in a region to minimize the impact to one particular airport, and Secret Service may also preposition a Gulfstream ___E:C-37B U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-37B)___ or ___E:Boeing E-4 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_E-4)___ in a neighboring region for backup.
In addition to the president, staff, and flight crew, a VC-25A can carry 102 guests in typical domestic business-class ___E:seats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airline_seat)___ .
The back-up VC-25 typically flies with 14 crew, two pilots, six flight crew, two cooks, and four flight attendants.

When transporting the president, the primary VC-25A has three cooks and 15 flight attendants, 20 or more Secret Service agents, and some 40 members of the presidential ___E:press pool U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_pool)___ .
During international state visits, another aircraft may be chartered to accommodate another 150 or more journalists and security personnel.

On ___E:11 September 2001 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ , George W. Bush was interrupted as he attended an event at ___E:Emma E. Booker Elementary School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_E._Booker_Elementary_School)___ in ___E:Sarasota, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarasota,_Florida)___ , after ___E:an airplane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Airlines_Flight_175)___ hit the South Tower of the ___E:World Trade Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(1973%E2%80%932001))___ in New York City. He took off on a VC-25 from ___E:Sarasota-Bradenton International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarasota-Bradenton_International_Airport)___ piloted by Colonel Mark Tillman, the senior pilot of Air Force One that day.
Some time later, air traffic controllers warned Tillman that a passenger jet was nearby and not responding to radio calls.
Tillman recalls: "As we got over ___E:Gainesville, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gainesville,_Florida)___ , we got the word from Jacksonville Center.

They said, 'Air Force One you have traffic behind you and basically above you that is descending into you, we are not in contact with them—they have shut their responder [ sic ] off.' And at that time it kind of led us to believe maybe someone was coming into us in Sarasota, they saw us take off, they just stayed high and are following us at this point.

We had no idea what the capabilities of the terrorists were at that point."  Tillman then flew Air Force One over the ___E:Gulf of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico)___ in order, he later said, to test whether the other aircraft would follow.

The other jet continued on its route, and Tillman said that it was later explained to him that an airliner had lost its ___E:transponder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transponder_(aeronautics))___ , which normally broadcasts an electronic identification signal, and that the pilots on board neglected to switch to another radio frequency.

Later, Tillman received a warning of an imminent attack on Air Force One. "We got word from the vice president and the staff that 'Angel was next,' indicating the classified call sign for Air Force One. Once we got into the Gulf [of Mexico] and they passed to us that 'Angel was next,' at that point I asked for fighter support.

If an airliner was part of the attack, it would be good to have fighters on the wing to go ahead and take care of us." At this point, Tillman said that the plan to fly the president back to Washington, D.C., was aborted for concerns that Air Force One would be attacked at ___E:Andrews Air Force Base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrews_Air_Force_Base)___ .

Instead, Tillman landed at ___E:Barksdale Air Force Base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barksdale_Air_Force_Base)___ , ___E:Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana)___ , and ___E:Offutt Air Force Base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offutt_Air_Force_Base)___ , ___E:Nebraska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska)___ , where the president made a speech.
After these stops, the president was returned to Washington, D.C.

The next day, officials at the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ and the ___E:Justice Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice)___ explained that President Bush did this because there was "specific and credible information that the White House and Air Force One were also intended targets".
The White House could not confirm evidence of a threat to Air Force One, and investigation found the original claim to be a result of miscommunication.
The VC-25As are to be replaced as the cost of maintaining the aging systems on their 30-year-old airframes and less efficient GE-CF6 engines has begun to surpass the cost of acquiring a new aircraft.
On 28 January 2015, the Air Force announced that the ___E:Boeing 747-8 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_747-8)___ would be the next presidential aircraft.

The US ___E:Government Accountability Office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_Accountability_Office)___ estimated the total cost at $3.2 billion, and the US Air Force's budget for the program is projected to be nearly $4 billion.
In December 2016, Boeing was on contract for preliminary development worth $170 million (~$217 million in 2024).
During his first presidency, Donald Trump renegotiated aspects of the contract with Boeing, and threatened to cancel the program if the overall cost exceeded $4 billion.

In an effort to cut costs, the Air Force contracted to purchase two completed but undelivered ___E:Transaero U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transaero)___ 747-8 intercontinental aircraft from Boeing in 2017.
The following year, Boeing struck a deal with Trump to adorn the new planes with a "patriotic color scheme" featuring a deep red stripe down the middle of the aircraft and a dark blue underbelly.

Plagued by multiple delays, and the rising cost of the aircraft, this color scheme was scrapped, and a modernized version of the classic Air Force One design was made public in March 2023. The first VC-25B is scheduled to be delivered in 2027, while the second will come the following year.

In September 2020, the US Air Force announced several Presidential and Executive Airlift Directorate contracts signed with aircraft manufacturers to begin development of a ___E:supersonic aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supersonic_aircraft)___ that could function as Air Force One. Contracts have been signed with ___E:Exosonic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exosonic)___ ,  ___E:Hermeus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermeus)___ ,   and ___E:Boom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boom_Technology)___ .

On 21 May 2025, the ___E:Trump administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump)___ accepted a ___E:Boeing 747-8 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_747-8)___ as a gift from the ___E:royal family of Qatar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Thani)___ .
The administration plans to use it as the new Air Force One. With an estimated value of US$400 million, this will be the most valuable gift extended to the US from a foreign government.
For this aircraft to be used as Air Force One, it will have to undergo extensive inspection and modifications to afford the protection to the president that current Air Force One aircraft provide.

These modifications will not be completed until after 2028.  On 28 May 2025, the Washington Post reported that no deal had been agreed because Qatar required a ___E:memorandum of understanding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorandum_of_understanding)___ confirming that any transfer request had been initiated by the US in order to ensure that Qatar had no legal liability.
On 7 July 2025, ___E:Pete Hegseth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Hegseth)___ signed the memorandum of understanding.

During the ___E:Johnson Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson_Administration)___ , the United States Air Force acquired a ___E:Beechcraft King Air B90 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beechcraft_King_Air#Air_Force_One)___ which was designated ___E:VC-6A U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beechcraft_King_Air#Air_Force_One)___ (66-7943).

The aircraft was used to transport ___E:President Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ between ___E:Bergstrom Air Force Base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergstrom_Air_Force_Base)___ and his family ranch near ___E:Johnson City, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_City,_Texas)___ ,  and was used at least once to transport the President to ___E:Princeton, New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton,_New_Jersey)___ .
It was referred to as Lady Bird's airplane and later in its service life featured a basic color scheme similar to civilian aircraft.
When the President was aboard, the aircraft used the call sign Air Force One.

___E:United Airlines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Airlines)___ is the only commercial airline to have operated Executive One , the call sign given to a civilian flight on which the US president is aboard.

On 26 December 1973, President ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ and his family flew as commercial passengers on a United ___E:DC-10 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC-10)___ from ___E:Washington Dulles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Dulles_International_Airport)___ to ___E:Los Angeles International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_International_Airport)___ .
His staff explained that this was done to conserve fuel by not having to fly the usual Boeing 707 Air Force aircraft.

In November 1999, President ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ flew from ___E:Ankara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankara)___ , Turkey, to ___E:Cengiz Topel Naval Air Station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cengiz_Topel_Naval_Air_Station)___ outside Izmit, Turkey, aboard a marked ___E:C-20C U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulfstream_III)___ (Gulfstream III) using the call sign Air Force One , escorted by three F-16s.

On 8 March 2000, President Clinton flew to Pakistan aboard an unmarked ___E:Gulfstream III U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulfstream_III)___ while another aircraft with the call sign Air Force One flew on the same route a few minutes later.
This diversion was reported by several US press outlets.

On 1 May 2003, President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ flew in the co-pilot seat of a Sea Control Squadron Thirty-Five ( ___E:VS-35 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VS-35_(1990%E2%80%932005))___ ) ___E:S-3B Viking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S-3_Viking)___ from ___E:Naval Air Station North Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_North_Island)___ , California to the aircraft carrier ___E:USS Abraham Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Abraham_Lincoln_(CVN-72))___ off the California coast, where Bush delivered his ___E:"Mission Accomplished" speech U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Mission_Accomplished_speech)___ .

During the flight, the aircraft used the call sign of " ___E:Navy One U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_One)___ " for the first time. This aircraft is now on display at the ___E:National Naval Aviation Museum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Naval_Aviation_Museum)___ at ___E:Naval Air Station Pensacola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Pensacola)___ , Florida.

___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ used the Gulfstream ___E:C-37 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulfstream_V#Variants)___ variant on a personal trip in 2009 to visit the production of ___E:August Wilson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_Wilson)___ 's Joe Turner's Come and Gone in New York.

Several ___E:Boeing C-17 Globemaster IIIs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_C-17_Globemaster_III)___ typically accompany the president whenever he travels, carrying the ___E:presidential limousines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_state_car_(United_States))___ and other support vehicles, and have been rumored to have discreetly transported presidents and vice presidents in and out of Iraq and Afghanistan without using the Air Force One call sign.

Since 1998, the president has occasionally flown aboard an Air Force ___E:C-32 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_C-32)___ , a ___E:narrow-body jet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrow-body_aircraft)___ based on the ___E:Boeing 757 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_757)___ airliner.
The Air Force bought four C-32s in 1996 to fly the president to airports whose runways were too small to accommodate the larger VC-25, or as emergency backup.
Today, these aircraft are used to fly vice presidents and other senior officials.
The C-32 has also been used by presidents when use of the VC-25 could present operational risks.
For example in 2023 when President Biden traveled to Ukraine via Poland using the C-32 to avoid the publicity of the VC-25.

In the 2010s, the Air Force acquired a second set of four 757s for presidential transport, assigning them tail numbers 90015, 90016, 90017, and 90018. Service officials do not acknowledge that these aircraft exist, although they are routinely photographed in presidential service.
Vice presidents have used a VC-25 on longer trips, using the Air Force Two call sign.
The president regularly flies in helicopters (call sign ___E:Marine One U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_One)___ ) operated by the U.S.
Marine Corps.

VC-137B SAM 970 , used from 1959 to 1962 as Air Force One and until 1996 in the presidential fleet, is on display at ___E:The Museum of Flight U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Museum_of_Flight)___ in ___E:Seattle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle)___ , Washington.
